web/composer/tools/sessions.py:R5:build_: R5 on `if isinstance(resolved, ToolResult):`. The value is Tier-1/2, not Tier-3: `resolved` is the return of `_resolve_source_blob`, whose annotation is the closed owned union `_ResolvedSourceBlob | ToolResult` -- two frozen dataclasses ELSPETH defines, neither of which is subclassed anywhere in `src/` or `tests/` (verified by importing every `elspeth.*` module and reading `ToolResult.__subclasses__()`, which is empty, and `_ResolvedSourceBlob.__mro__`, which is `(_ResolvedSourceBlob, object)`). This is therefore the nominal discrimination of an owned errors-as-return-values union that ADR-032 prescribes -- `isinstance` against a concrete class we define -- and not a shape guard over external data. It is not converted to the house exact-type idiom `type(resolved) is ToolResult` because mypy gives `type(x) is C` NO negative-branch narrowing on a union (measured: a three-case probe where the `isinstance` form checks clean and both `type() is` orderings raise `union-attr` / `arg-type` on the negative branch), so the swap re-types the three following reads -- `resolved_source_blob = resolved`, `resolved.plugin`, `resolved.options` -- back to the bare union and loses the static proof that the success arm is a `_ResolvedSourceBlob`. Trading real type checking for a lint-shape change would hide more than it reveals. What it protects: the blob-resolution failure arm. When resolution fails, `_resolve_source_blob` returns a populated rejection `ToolResult`, and this branch routes it to `_candidate(resolved)` so the failure reaches the planner as a repairable candidate rejection instead of being read as a resolved source.
web/composer/tools/sessions.py:R6:build_: R6 on `except ValueError as exc:` around `canonical_sink_local_paths(output.options)`. The value is Tier-3: `output.options` is an LLM/planner-authored sink option block arriving as `set_pipeline` tool-call arguments, and `canonical_sink_local_paths` raises `ValueError` for an option the planner may legitimately author wrong (a bare relative sink path containing '..' segments, which must not be rooted into the managed outputs pool). The handler is not a swallow: it converts the rejection into the explicit, planner-repairable error result the tool contract requires, and this loop is the per-component collector, so a `raise` here would abandon the remaining outputs' checks and return one defect where the planner needs the full repair set. Controls, by symbol: (1) `_record_component_rejection` appends `_failure_result(state, f"Output '{output.sink_name}': {exc}", error_code="plugin_options_invalid")` -- the exception text reaches the planner under a closed error code, nothing is discarded; (2) `uncanonical_output_indexes` records the index so the second `enumerate(validated.outputs)` loop `continue`s past it rather than reading the absent `canonical_out_options[index]`, which is what keeps the swallow from degrading into a later KeyError on a half-canonicalised output; (3) `_collected_component_failure` merges every recorded rejection into the returned `SetPipelineCandidate`, whose `acceptable` is then false, so neither caller can mistake the handled ValueError for success -- `pipeline_planner.plan_pipeline` raises `_PipelineCandidateRejected(candidate.result)` and `tool_batch` raises `AuditIntegrityError` on an unacceptable candidate. What it protects: the S2 sink-path allowlist. An output whose paths did not canonicalise is excluded from the trusted `canonical_out_options` map, so no unvalidated path can reach `_validate_sink_path` or the stored `OutputSpec` by way of this handler.
